questions.stem:
A balloon shop had \(150\) balloons in the morning, \(30\) of which were filled with helium.

During the day, \(\frac{1}{5}\) of the helium balloons were sold and \(15\) of the ordinary balloons were accidentally popped. What fraction of the balloons left at the end of the day were filled with helium?
questions.hint: Calculate the number of helium and ordinary balloons left.
questions.solution:
Helium sold = $\frac{1}{5} \times 30 = 6$. Helium left = $30 - 6 = 24$.
Ordinary started = $150 - 30 = 120$.
Ordinary popped = $15$. Ordinary left = $120 - 15 = 105$.
Total left = $24 + 105 = 129$.
Fraction = $\frac{24}{129} = \frac{8}{43}$.

questions.stem: If Alice can swim \(100\text{ m}\) backstroke in \(1\text{ minute } 15\text{ seconds}\) and she can swim butterfly at \(\frac{5}{4}\) times her backstroke speed, and freestyle at \(\frac{6}{5}\) times her butterfly speed, how fast can she swim \(100\text{ m}\) freestyle?
questions.hint: Use the inverse relationship between speed and time.
questions.solution:
Speed is inversely proportional to time.
Backstroke time = $75\text{ s}$.
Butterfly time = $75 \div \frac{5}{4} = 75 \times \frac{4}{5} = 60\text{ s}$.
Freestyle time = $60 \div \frac{6}{5} = 60 \times \frac{5}{6} = 50\text{ s}$.
